grade.rationale: The stylesheet is coherent and consistently uses shared design tokens, but the folder table has a responsive overflow defect that can make columns inaccessible.

summary: The styling is generally well structured and maintainable. One confirmed correctness issue causes the folder table's fixed 1120px grid to be clipped without horizontal scrolling in narrower containers. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied, and the unavailable ESLint run provides no applicable CSS findings.

grade.rationale: Most layout rules are internally consistent, but the folder viewport can permanently hide columns when its available width is below the grid's 1120px minimum.
Selectors are logically grouped and design tokens are used consistently, although tightly packed declarations make future layout changes somewhat harder to inspect.
Class names clearly communicate component roles and states, but the interaction between the table's minimum widths and overflow rules is not self-evident.
Error handling has limited applicability to CSS; state-specific styling and empty-state presentation are present, with no separate failure-state defect identified.
The component-oriented selectors are suitable for viewport and visual-regression testing. Coverage remains unknown because no coverage evidence was provided.

findings.title: Folder table columns can be clipped with no way to reach them
findings.description: The header and rows require at least 1120px of width, while the viewport declares a smaller 980px minimum and explicitly hides horizontal overflow. When the containing pane is narrower than 1120px, the rightmost columns extend beyond the visible area but no horizontal scrollbar is available, making their content and controls inaccessible.
findings.recommendation: Allow horizontal scrolling on the viewport with `overflow-x:auto`, and place both the column header and rows inside the same scrolling element so they remain horizontally aligned. Alternatively, replace the fixed minimum-width grid with a responsive column layout that fits the supported minimum pane width.
